- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2% above recent peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently underestimates true mean reversion in 30-day horizon; if 30d forecast is below 70.00 and sentiment is neutral/positive, adjust up by 0.5–1.5%.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model tends to lag; forecast should be 1–2 days ahead of true trend, not lagging.
- If 30d forecast is >73.00 and sentiment is neutral or negative, reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid overconfidence in upward momentum.
- If 30d forecast is <70.00 and sentiment is positive, model often fails to recover; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to capture sentiment-driven rebound.
